hands.decision: Top pair in a squeezed pot facing a 2/3-pot river bet after a doubled-size turn barrel on a scary river: call or fold?
hands.what_happened: Mariano folded; villain showed 77. Rated 5/7.
hands.commentary: Squeeze linear (good, better, best) when there is an open and a call because you will see a flop often; QTo is a couple pips too loose. Double barrel exactly double the previous size on a nut-changing card is weighted to bluffs, but players rarely bluff third pair (77 on the 6) and many draws got there, so the fold is fine. Don't use 'no spade in my hand' as a crutch; use the bluff-catching checklist: is the player capable, is the size significant, do they have non-showdown hands. Players who show bluffs are under-bluffers.

Gethin called flop, donked $250 on the turn (both called), then bet $800 into ~$1,000 on the river; LJ snap-folded (A3 of spades, missed flush draw), HJ called with AKo and lost.
hands.commentary: Mark: Todd's flop fold is a bit tight and he jumped to an action without weighing options. Josiah planned the SPR well on the turn but got too zoomed in on monsters on the river; Mark wanted a river value bet targeting AA, AK, KQ. Gethin planned ahead (rec won't double/triple barrel enough, so call wider on flop) and found the river bet; he said a slightly bigger turn (300-350) could have set up all the money on the river. Mark's model had AK calling up to ~400-500 on the turn.

hands.what_happened: Todd donked $50, LJ raised to $150, CO called, Todd called; turn 9d he checked, LJ bet $300, CO raised to $700, Todd folded. Josiah checked, LJ bet $50, CO called, he check-raised $325, both called; turn he bet $650, LJ called, CO jammed, Josiah folded.
